**U.S. assembly‑plant openings for the three automakers**

| Automaker | Brand that built the engine / owned the brand | First U.S. assembly plant (location) | Year it opened / first vehicle rolled off |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| **Honda** | *VTEC* ‑ Honda’s variable‑valve‑timing system (engine) | Marysville, Ohio plant | **1979** – the Marysville Auto Plant started production in 1979 and was Honda’s first U.S. factory. |
| **Toyota** | *Scion* ‑ Toyota’s former sub‑brand | Georgetown, Kentucky (Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky) | **1988** – the Kentucky plant began production in May 1988 (groundbreaking 1986). It was Toyota’s first wholly‑owned U.S. vehicle plant. |
| **Nissan** | – | Smyrna, Tennessee (Nissan Motor Manufacturing Corp.) | **1983** – the Smyrna plant first produced a vehicle (a white 720 pickup) in June 1983; it was Nissan’s first U.S. assembly plant. |

**Sources**

* Honda: The Honda website’s “U.S. Manufacturing” page notes that “Honda began manufacturing in America in 1979, opening our first plant in Marysville, Ohio.” (© 2025).
* Toyota: Toyota’s press‑release for the Kentucky plant states the plant “broke ground in Georgetown, Kentucky, in May 1986, and two years later (May 1988), produced its first Camry.” (Date of press release: 2026‑11‑06).
* Nissan: Nissan’s own news release, “40 Years of People, Product and Purpose,” states that “the first Nissan manufactured in the U.S. – a white 720 pickup – rolled off the assembly line in Smyrna, Tennessee, on June 16, 1983.” (Date of release: 2023‑05‑17).

## Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky

Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky is Toyota’s largest vehicle manufacturing plant in the world, capable of producing 550,000 vehicles and more than 600,000 engines annually. Toyota broke ground in Georgetown, Kentucky, in May of 1986, and two years later (May 1988), produced its first Camry. Since then, more than 14 million vehicles have rolled off Toyota’s assembly lines in Kentucky, where full-time employment is 10,000. In addition to the Camry Hybrid, America’s best-selling car, Toyota Kentucky also manufactures the RAV4 Hybrid, as well as four-cylinder and V-6 engines. Toyota has invested more than $164 million in various community philanthropic and educational initiatives since 1986.

**U.S. assembly‑plant openings for the three automakers**

| Automaker | Brand that built the engine / owned the brand | First U.S. assembly plant (location) | Year it opened / first vehicle rolled off |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| **Honda** | *VTEC* ‑ Honda’s variable‑valve‑timing system (engine) | Marysville, Ohio plant | **1979** – the Marysville Auto Plant started production in 1979 and was Honda’s first U.S. factory. |
| **Toyota** | *Scion* ‑ Toyota’s former sub‑brand | Georgetown, Kentucky (Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky) | **1988** – the Kentucky plant began production in May 1988 (groundbreaking 1986). It was Toyota’s first wholly‑owned U.S. vehicle plant. |
| **Nissan** | – | Smyrna, Tennessee (Nissan Motor Manufacturing Corp.) | **1983** – the Smyrna plant first produced a vehicle (a white 720 pickup) in June 1983; it was Nissan’s first U.S. assembly plant. |

**Sources**

* Honda: The Honda website’s “U.S. Manufacturing” page notes that “Honda began manufacturing in America in 1979, opening our first plant in Marysville, Ohio.” (© 2025).
* Toyota: Toyota’s press‑release for the Kentucky plant states the plant “broke ground in Georgetown, Kentucky, in May 1986, and two years later (May 1988), produced its first Camry.” (Date of press release: 2026‑11‑06).
* Nissan: Nissan’s own news release, “40 Years of People, Product and Purpose,” states that “the first Nissan manufactured in the U.S. – a white 720 pickup – rolled off the assembly line in Smyrna, Tennessee, on June 16, 1983.” (Date of release: 2023‑05‑17).
